title: Mutes, matching sounds, and Stan Kenton's Ellington imitation
summary: Brass sections cut mute corks to match; Kenton tried for Ellington's sound but Duke's plunger effects confused white musicians.

Now you was talking about using a cork mute and a mellow mute. That's what whatchamacallem was trying to do on the coast.
Stan Kenton. He was trying to get the Duke Ellington sound, but Duke Ellington never used anything like that.
See, Duke would use a mute -- plunger mute -- and trumpet. They'd tighten them up and blow. Open up just a little bit. Get that sound, you know. (humming notes)
And all of a sudden, they loosen the thing and they attack the note, pow, you know. And they [whistle yell] (inaudible), you know.
And a lot of those things really puzzled a lot of white musicians, because they didn't know what was going on.
